subject: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up + proposed POC plan (model selection)

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped and started: 

Summary of goals / success criteria (from our notes):
- Entity extraction F1 >= 0.92 on your annotated dataset
- Mean latency (p95) < 300ms for 512-token requests
- Spanish support for customer messages (primary) + English support
- Cost target: average inference cost under $0.015 per 1k tokens (goal, flexible)

Model candidates we're proposing for the trial:
1) Llama2-13B-chat (quantized) — balance of quality & cost; good multilingual baseline
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B — strong instruction-following and lower cost; good fallback option
3) Mistral-8x / or larger open model (if you want higher quality for edge cases)

Recommended default for the POC: Llama2-13B-chat (primary), with Mistral-Instruct-7B as a fallback variant for cost-sensitive routes. If Spanish performance needs extra attention we'll include a tuned run and focused eval set.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): sign off on success criteria & data access (we'll need a 500–1k sample labeled set to start)
- Week 1: infra + baseline runs (Redwood will provision trial endpoints and run baseline evals)
- Week 2: model variations (quantization, smaller fallback) + latency tuning
- Week 3: final evaluation & recap; decision on production rollout

Ownership: Redwood (Ben + Marissa) will run the baseline evaluations and provide results; Acme will provide labeled eval set and any privacy/ingestion constraints (Diego/Sofia).

Deliverables we will provide:
- Evaluation report (metrics: F1, precision, recall, latency, cost)
- Config suggestions (batching, cache, quantization) to hit latency/cost targets

Attachments: POC_Eval_Criteria.xlsx (we'll update with the specific labels and examples)

Can you confirm the success criteria above and the timeline? If that's good, we'll get the NDA & data transfer steps moving and schedule a kickoff for next Monday.

Best,
Ben

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acmeai.com>

Cc: Diego Ramirez <diego@acmeai.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:41:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed POC plan (model selection)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Success criteria: F1 >= 0.92 is correct (we can be flexible +/- 0.01 depending on latency tradeoffs).
- Multilingual: Spanish support is critical — about 35% of our traffic is Spanish. We'll need to see per-language metrics in the report.
- Latency target p95 < 300ms is non-negotiable for the real-time route. For async batch workflows we can accept higher latency with the smaller model.
- Fallback model: yes, we want a smaller cheaper fallback for low-value routes; the Mistral-Instruct-7B sounds reasonable.

Data: we'll share a 750-sample labeled set (mix of English/Spanish) by Monday. I'll upload via the shared Drive link and loop Diego for any privacy questions.

NDA: attached (signed) — see NDA_signed.pdf.

Kickoff: Monday works for a 30-minute kickoff (we prefer 10:00am PT).

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Martinez
Head of ML Product
Acme AI

Sofia —

Perfect, thanks for the confirmation and for the signed NDA. Quick notes based on your replies and our infra constraints: 

1) Multilingual evaluation: we'll split the eval set by language and report per-language F1 + combined metrics. We'll also run a small Spanish-only fine-tune / prompt-tuning pass if baseline falls short.

2) Fallback routing: we'll provide two endpoint configs —
   - real-time route (p95 < 300ms) using Llama2-13B-chat quantized + aggressive batching/caching
   - low-cost route using Mistral-Instruct-7B (smaller) for non-critical flows

3) Timeline update & owners: 
   - Today: Redwood (Marissa) will provision trial endpoints and request data access.
   - Tue (Mar 3): baseline runs on both models; initial latency profile.
   - Wed-Fri (Mar 4-6): tuning and quantized runs; generate evaluation report by end of week.
